newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador Congress raises corporate income tax.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador Congress raises corporate income tax.

text.p: Ecuador's Congress has voted to raise income tax paid by companies, a congressional spokesman said Thursday.

Congress late Wednesday approved a partial presidential veto to earlier tax legislation, backing changes to the ICE tax on special consumption and raising income tax to 25 percent from 20 percent, the source told Reuters.
The new tax law favors tobacco, liquor and car manufacturers, reducing their ICE payments.
Tax on cigarettes made from blonde tobacco will be lowered to 75 percent from 103 percent and that on cigarettes with black tabacco to 18 percent from 48 percent.
Liquor tax was cut to 26 percent from 43 percent.
The law, which will be enacted over the next few days, does not specify how much the government hopes to collect in new revenues but legislators estimate that amount at $149 million (600,000 sucres).
Ecuador's fiscal deficit is running at six percent of gross domestic product.
